title: JWT key confusion in a small API
summary: How an algorithm mismatch turned a harmless token check into account access.
body: A compact lab about reading the verification path before reaching for a payload.
<Callout type="note">Always pin the accepted signing algorithm in server configuration.</Callout>
The useful clue was the branch that selected the verification key.
Pin allowed algorithms and test rejection paths as well as valid tokens.

title: Cache me if you can
summary: A cache key that forgot the Host header made the response reusable in the wrong place.
body: This challenge was a reminder that caches have their own idea of identity.
I compared requests through the proxy and saw that a response generated for one host could be replayed for another.
Keep cache keys aligned with every input that changes the response.

title: Notes on Linux capabilities
summary: A field checklist for understanding what a process can do beyond its UID.
body: Capabilities split traditional root privileges into smaller permissions. During an assessment, inventory both file capabilities and the capabilities held by running processes.
Use `getcap` to find file capabilities, then check whether the binary can be influenced through arguments, environment, or writable paths.
Trace the process context and inputs before treating a capability as exploitable.
